newsitem.title: JAPAN: Showa Shell unit to start gas oil desulphuriser.
newsitem.headline: Showa Shell unit to start gas oil desulphuriser.

text.p: Showa Yokkaichi Sekiyu Co Ltd said on Thursday it would start operating a 28,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) gas oil desulphurisation unit on Friday.
The new unit will be able to produce gas oil with sulphur content of 0.05 percent when the government toughens quality restrictions next year, Showa Yokkaichi said.
The government plans to lower the maximum allowable sulphur content in gas oil to 0.05 percent in October 1997 from the current 0.2 percent.
Showa Yokkaichi Sekiyu is a subsidiary of Showa Shell Sekiyu KK, which is owned 50 percent by the Royal Dutch/Shell Group.

A company spokesman said that for the time being, the new unit would produce gas oil meeting current quality restrictions and that it was unclear when the unit would start producing gas oil meeting the more stringent requirements.
Earlier this month, Showa Yokkaichi started commercial operation of a 240,000 bpd residue fluid catalytic cracker, which produces gasoline, gas oil and kerosene from fuel oil.
